items.description: The stated clamp coordinate x=0 conflicts with the left boundary x=-1 of the specified domain and the illustrated left-edge clamp.
readings: Clamp the full left edge x=-1, -0.5<y<0.5.
Clamp the internal full-height line x=0, -0.5<y<0.5, following the stated Gamma_D literally.
items.evidence: Sec. 4.1.1 specifies Omega=(-1,1)x(-0.5,0.5), but the cantilever paragraph gives Gamma_D={0}x(-0.5,0.5). Fig. 4(a) shows the left edge clamped.

items.description: The load is called a point load, but its prescribed Neumann set is a finite segment.
readings: Apply a concentrated downward force at (1,0).
Apply uniform downward traction over x=1, -0.05<y<0.05.
items.evidence: Sec. 4.1.1, cantilever paragraph: downward point load at the right-edge center, with Gamma_N={1}x(-0.05,0.05). Sec. 3.2.1, Eqs. (3.16)-(3.17), integrates traction over Gamma_N.

items.description: The stated unit load can mean a unit resultant force or unit traction intensity on the specified segment.
readings: Total downward force is 1, interpreting (0,-1) as a point-force vector.
Total downward force is 0.1 per unit thickness, interpreting (0,-1) as uniform traction on the segment of length 0.1.
items.evidence: Sec. 4.1.1 calls t=(0,-1)^T a point load while prescribing a finite Gamma_N; Eqs. (3.16)-(3.17) use t as boundary traction.
